title: A New UK Porn Ban Sparks Fears of Unprecedented Sex Censorship
gist: From November 6, UK Crime and Policing Act amendments criminalize possessing or publishing porn depicting strangulation/suffocation, 'fauxcest' and role-play as minors, with penalties of up to five years in prison. Experts warn the broad wording could sweep in mainstream niches and put the UK-based OnlyFans parent Fenix International in the crosshairs, and that similar laws are being discussed in Italy, the Netherlands, Spain and among US evangelical lobbyists.

themes.theme: Scope of the new UK law

insights.claim: From November 6, amendments to the UK Crime and Policing Act outlaw possessing or publishing pornographic images of strangulation or suffocation, with violations punishable by up to five years in prison and a fine.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Making possession a crime raises the legal risk for UK users and for platforms with a UK presence.
insights.quote: possession or publication of pornographic images of strangulation or suffocation

insights.claim: The law also bans 'fauxcest' (simulated sex between non-blood family members) and performers role-playing as minors under 16, following a review by Conservative peer Baroness Gabby Bertin that cited anecdotal evidence of fauxcest being used to enable child abuse.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Fauxcest is described as an extremely popular niche, so a ban removes a large slice of catalog and revenue.

insights.claim: The law defines possession as an image stored on a phone, a hard drive or in cloud storage.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Cloud providers and device users could be exposed, and so could foreign creators who travel to the UK.
insights.locator: Though the law currently applies only

insights.claim: A UK obscenity lawyer argues the suffocation wording is broad enough that face-sitting and even oral sex could arguably count, meaning 'the UK could have just banned blow jobs' in online porn.
insights.speaker: Myles Jackman
insights.so_what: Unclear legal boundaries push platforms to over-remove content to stay compliant.
insights.quote: the UK could have just banned blow jobs

insights.claim: Jackman calls the law one of the greatest acts of suppression of free speech in global history.
insights.speaker: Myles Jackman
insights.so_what: A sign of how strongly the adult industry and civil liberties groups will push back.
insights.quote: it genuinely seems like one of the greatest acts of suppression of free speech in global history

insights.claim: A creator warns that the AI image-recognition software platforms already use widely could flag content that does not actually violate the law, because it takes a heavy-handed approach.
insights.speaker: Alexandra Snow
insights.so_what: AI moderation false positives under strict liability rules could hurt creator earnings and platform volume.
insights.quote: They use a very broad, heavy-handed approach
insights.locator: Snow says she is particularly concerned

insights.claim: IWantClips has already published new UK guidelines and removed clips in categories including 'breast smothering', 'jeans facesitting' and 'scissorhold'.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Platforms are complying ahead of enforcement and removing content, which shrinks UK-accessible catalogs.
insights.locator: In advance of the new legislation

insights.claim: A US OnlyFans creator estimates 60-70% of her content involves role-play, including step-'fauxcest', and argues the ban will push worse, actually illegal content underground.
insights.speaker: Cami Strella
insights.so_what: Shows how large a share of creator revenue is exposed, and the risk of displacement to unregulated channels.
insights.quote: it’ll just push even worse content that is actually illegal or immoral underground

insights.claim: A UK dominatrix says she is removing videos from IWantClips and OnlyFans and expects a large financial hit once the law takes effect.
insights.speaker: Trans Princess Jezebel
insights.so_what: Creator income loss feeds directly into platform take-rate revenue.

insights.claim: An adult-industry attorney says OnlyFans is especially vulnerable because its parent Fenix International Limited is based in the UK, unlike most US porn companies, which Ofcom finds hard to reach.
insights.speaker: Michael Fattorosi
insights.so_what: Concentrated regulatory risk for the largest creator platform, owing to where it is domiciled.
insights.quote: If I were OnlyFans,” Fattorosi says, “I’d be very worried about this.

insights.claim: Ofcom has already fined OnlyFans for failing to answer information requests about its age-check measures accurately, and it can fine sites up to 10% of worldwide revenue.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Penalties based on worldwide revenue make UK enforcement material to OnlyFans' finances.

insights.claim: Fattorosi advises creators visiting the UK on holiday or for conferences to be careful about what they keep on their phones.
insights.speaker: Michael Fattorosi
insights.so_what: The law's reach goes beyond UK borders in practice.

insights.claim: Jackman says lawmakers in Italy, the Netherlands and Spain, and US evangelical lobbyists, are discussing similar legislation, so the UK may not remain an outlier.
insights.speaker: Myles Jackman
insights.so_what: Similar laws in multiple countries would enlarge the market exposed to adult-platform content restrictions.
insights.quote: the lights are going out across the globe

insights.claim: The UK Ministry of Justice says the laws target content that normalizes violence against women, as part of a commitment to halve violence against women and girls within a decade.
insights.speaker: UK Ministry of Justice
insights.so_what: The government frames the law as fighting violence, which makes reversal politically unlikely.
insights.quote: We’re committed to halving violence against women and girls in a decade
insights.locator: In a statement sent to WIRED

insights.claim: Unlike the US, where Section 230 largely exempts platforms from liability for hosted content, the UK has a long record of strict restrictions on online porn.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: The gap between the US and UK liability regimes determines where platforms face regulatory risk.
